title: Brahmandapurana, book 2
source: sa_brahmANDapurANa.txt; GRETIL (gretil.sub.uni-goettingen.de), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (data entry: members of the Sansknet Project)
reply:
Only a few verses state a kinship relation.

- 2,73.28: Bṛhaspati calls the other "bhrāto 'yamaṅgirāḥ", meaning "this is the Āṅgirasa, my brother". The text is garbled. The clearest reading takes "bhrāto 'yam" as "brother", but the speaker is Bṛhaspati speaking to the asuras, so the claim is part of the impersonation and not a reliable statement. I leave it out.
- 2,73.52: "pautrastava punarbaliḥ" says Bali is the grandson of the person addressed, who is Kāvya/Śukra (the verse addresses "tubhyam"). So Bali is a descendant of Śukra, though the Sanskrit word is pautra. The speaker is Brahmā and the addressee is Kāvya. Prahlāda is addressed in 2,73.44-46, and Kāvya replies from 2,73.47 on, so "tava" in 2,73.52 refers to Kāvya or Śukra. Strictly the word "pautra" means a son's son, and the text elsewhere makes Bali the grandson of Prahlāda. Here the verses say only that he is the pautra of the addressee. In the text's own words, this is a statement that Bali is Śukra's grandson, so I record it as descendant_of with doubt true.
- 2,73.53: "pautraste brahmaṇā svayam" repeats the point, but one statement per relation is enough.
- 2,73.13: "diteḥ sutāḥ" makes the Daityas sons of Diti. The verse names them only as a group ("sarve diteḥ sutāḥ"), so I record the group as "Daityas".
- 2,73.8: "māhendrī tvam" calls Jayantī Indra's daughter. The word "māhendrī" means "of Mahendra", and the verse addresses her as such. Elsewhere in this text she is called Jayantī, and she is addressed in 2,73.3 as the one being spoken to. I record her as daughter_of Mahendra with doubt true.
